brand.name: Gravel & Gasket Mobile Mechanic
brand.tagline: The shop comes to your driveway.

owner.name: Silas Renner
owner.heading: The guy in the driveway
owner.bio: Silas Renner learned the trade the way a lot of small-town mechanics do: fixing whatever showed up in the yard, because the nearest shop was forty minutes and a tow bill away. Gravel & Gasket started as a toolbox in the back of a pickup and a habit of saying yes to neighbors, and it still runs on the same rule — if it can be done properly where it sits, it gets done where it sits, and if it cannot, you get told that plainly instead of expensively.

pricing.label: Oil & filter change
features: Full synthetic or conventional, your call
New filter, level set and top-off
Drip mat down — your concrete stays your concrete
pricing.note: Diesels and large-sump engines get their own number before we come out.

pricing.label: Brake pads & rotors
features: Torqued to spec, bedded in on a road test
Old parts left with you if you want them
pricing.note: We measure the corner and text you the number before a single part gets ordered.

pricing.label: Battery — tested, then replaced
features: Battery, alternator output and parasitic drain tested first
Terminals cleaned, hold-down replaced if it is rotten
pricing.note: If the battery tests healthy, you pay the diagnostic and nothing else.

pricing.label: Starter or alternator
features: Bolt-on replacement in your own parking space
Charging system re-checked after the swap
Belt and tensioner inspected while we are in there
pricing.note: Some engine bays are a two-hour job, some a five. Your quote says which.

pricing.label: Serpentine belt & tensioner
features: Squeal traced before anything gets replaced
Belt, tensioner and idler pulleys checked together
pricing.note: Belt alone, without the tensioner, lands at the bottom of that range.

pricing.label: Scan-tool diagnostic
pricing.per: waived if we do the repair
features: Codes pulled and live data read at the port
Road test with you in the passenger seat
Written finding, texted the same day
pricing.note: Book this one when the symptom is a light, a smell or a noise you cannot name.

pricing.label: Something not on this list
pricing.note: Send year, make, model and symptoms. Not a driveway job? We say so.

services.title: Brakes at the curb
services.desc: Pads, rotors and hardware, torqued to spec on your own driveway. The squeal you have been ignoring is an afternoon at home, not a week without your vehicle.

services.title: Batteries & charging
services.desc: We test before we sell: battery health, alternator output, and the parasitic drain that quietly kills a good battery in a month. Then we replace what actually failed.

services.title: Oil, filters & fluids
services.desc: Full synthetic or conventional, a new filter, and every level checked while the hood is up. The mat goes down first and the old oil leaves with us.

services.title: Starters, alternators & belts
services.desc: The bolt-on failures that strand people at the worst moment. Most of them come off and go back on right where the vehicle already sits.

services.title: Scan-tool diagnostics
services.desc: Check-engine lights, misfires, mystery drains. We plug in, road test with you riding along, and tell you the actual fault instead of the most expensive possibility.

services.title: Workplace & multi-vehicle visits
services.desc: Several vehicles at one address is one trip and one arrival window. Ask about a route stop for a whole work lot instead of booking them one at a time.

faq.q: What do you need at my house?
faq.a: A flat, reasonably level place to work beside the vehicle — a driveway, a carport pad, a parking space. We bring the tools, the jack, the stands, the lighting and a mat for the ground. Power and water are ours too.

faq.q: What if it turns out to need a real shop?
faq.a: Then we say so. Anything wanting a lift, an alignment rack, a paint booth or a transmission on a jack is not a driveway job, and pretending otherwise would cost you twice. You get told what it needs and where it should go.

faq.q: Do you work in apartment lots and business lots?
faq.a: Usually, with the property manager's blessing. Send the address first and we will tell you honestly whether the spot works before you go asking anyone.

faq.q: Can you do it while I am at work?
faq.a: That is a big part of the day. Leave the keys where we agree and you get texts and photos as it goes — most people walk out at the end of a shift to a vehicle that is already fixed.

faq.q: Do you supply the parts, or can I?
faq.a: Either way. We usually source them so our workmanship promise covers the whole job. Bring your own and we will still fit them — the promise then covers our labor only, and we put that in writing before starting.

faq.q: What happens if the weather turns?
faq.a: Rain and snow move brake and belt work; a battery or a scan handles almost anything. If the forecast would make the job worse, we call and move it rather than doing it badly.

faq.q: How do I pay, and is there a deposit?
faq.a: No deposit to book. Card or tap on the phone before we pull away, or an invoice by text if that suits you better.

hero.title: Your driveway is the shop bay.
hero.subtitle: Gravel & Gasket is a mobile mechanic working out of a loaded truck across Payette and the lower valley. Brakes, batteries, belts, oil and scan-tool diagnostics, done where the vehicle already sits — with a flat rate texted to you before we load up.

proof.small: It gets fixed where it sits
Stay home or stay at work

trust.title: Flat rate before the truck loads

about.heading: A shop bay is mostly just a floor with a roof over it
about.body: Most of what a vehicle asks for in a normal year — pads, rotors, a battery, a belt, fluids, a scan tool plugged into the port under the dash — does not need a lift, a lobby, or your car sleeping in somebody else's lot for three days. It needs a mechanic, a jack, a torque wrench and a flat patch of ground. That is the whole idea here: the truck comes to the vehicle, and you keep your keys and your day.
points: Nothing gets towed and nothing waits in a queue behind somebody else's transmission.
Watch the whole job over our shoulder if you want to — the old part goes in your hand or your bin, your call.
The flat rate arrives by text before we load the truck, and it does not move unless you approve a change.
Work parking lots count. Plenty of jobs get finished between clock-in and lunch.

process.title: Text what it is doing
process.desc: Year, make, model and the symptom. A photo, or a ten-second video of the noise, beats a paragraph every single time.

process.title: Get a flat rate back
process.desc: The price, the parts and roughly how long the truck will be in your driveway. Nothing is booked until you say yes to that number.

process.title: We roll up to you
process.desc: House, apartment lot, jobsite, work parking space — anywhere we can safely put jack stands on level ground.

process.title: Fixed, cleaned up, gone
process.desc: Photos of the old part, the drip mat picked up, and the invoice on your phone before we pull off your street.

niche.pricingNote: Flat rates, not moving targets. The number that arrives by text is the number on the invoice. The ranges cover the honest difference between a small sedan and a three-quarter-ton truck — your vehicle gets one number before we load up, and it only changes if you approve the change.
niche.pricePickerHint: Tap a service to load it into the quote line.

beforeAfter.heading: The two ends of one brake job
beforeAfter.blurb: Drag the divider. On the left, a hub carrier crusted over after a winter of road salt and gravel dust. On the right, what a fresh rotor looks like bolted up and ready to bed in on the road test.
beforeAfter.note: These are two different vehicles, photographed to show the two ends of the same job — not a before and after of one car. A real pair from your own driveway goes here once we have shot one.

book.heading: Tell us what it is doing
book.blurb: Takes about a minute: year, make, model, the symptom, and where the vehicle is sitting. A flat rate comes back by text, usually the same day, and nothing is booked until you say go.
book.buttonLabel: Send it — get my flat rate
book.doneHeading: Got it — the truck is in the loop
